reason: Both conversations correctly lead with a firm stop-using, don't-reset, don't-open-the-case warning and escalate to an engineer, and both lean unhelpfully toward the magnetron/capacitor as the 'likely' cause. Conversation 1 does more useful work: it names the door interlock switches as a plausible live-to-earth leakage source (close to the hidden truth), asks a relevant question that surfaces the shared extension lead with the kettle, elicits the 'bang from inside' detail, and reaffirms the stop and engineer route in a second turn. Conversation 2 is a single boilerplate turn that asks nothing, misses the interlock/door possibility entirely, and offers no path forward beyond 'call someone'. Neither asked the key test of whether the RCD stays set with the microwave unplugged nor mentioned that a cheap solo microwave is likely a replace-not-repair case, so the margin is clear rather than decisive.
